question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in San Francisco, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1979; the West Coast's most internationally significant photography-centred gallery, with Diane Arbus, Sophie Calle, Lee Friedlander, Richard Learoyd and Elisheva Biernoff, and a constant art-fair and museum presence.
notes.openai: Internationally authoritative photography and contemporary-art programme, with major museum placements and blue-chip artists.

notes.anthropic: The city's most ambitious younger blue-chip dealer; Woody De Othello, Rupy C. Tut, Judy Chicago, Clare Rojas and Hayal Pozanti, with placements in major museum collections and top-tier fairs.
notes.openai: Globally visible programme known for conceptually rigorous artists, strong museum relationships and major art-fair participation.

notes.anthropic: John Berggruen's gallery, since 1970 the city's leading dealer in postwar and modern masters alongside a strong contemporary roster; purpose-built Hawthorne Street space.
notes.openai: A leading West Coast gallery combining postwar masters with prominent contemporary artists and substantial institutional reach.

notes.anthropic: Critically the sharpest contemporary programme in the city — Trevor Paglen, K.r.m. Mooney, Liam Everett, Shannon Ebner — with consistent biennial and museum crossover.
notes.openai: Critically respected gallery representing conceptually ambitious emerging and established artists with international exposure.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1987; Andy Goldsworthy, Zhan Wang, Ai Weiwei projects and leading Bay Area artists, now anchoring Minnesota Street Project after decades at 49 Geary.
notes.openai: A durable, museum-facing programme especially strong in conceptual photography, installation and socially engaged practices.

notes.anthropic: Since 1991 a pioneer of new-media and politically engaged art, with the Media Room video programme and artists such as Masami Teraoka, Sandow Birk and Stephanie Syjuco.
notes.openai: Long-running gallery recognized for feminist, political and multimedia practices and sustained institutional advocacy.

notes.anthropic: Kathan Brown's etching workshop and gallery since 1962; editions with Diebenkorn, Kentridge, Marioni, Julie Mehretu and Tomma Abts make it a historic engine of Bay Area art.
notes.openai: World-renowned print publisher and gallery whose collaborations with major artists have shaped contemporary printmaking.

notes.anthropic: Collection-based international nonprofit with residencies, commissions and a globally networked exhibition and video programme.
notes.openai: The San Francisco base of a global contemporary-art organization, commissioning exhibitions and research with international artists.

notes.anthropic: Scholarly programme around Leonora Carrington, Remedios Varo and contemporary artists including Chitra Ganesh and María Magdalena Campos-Pons; pioneered a roving 'offsite' exhibition model.
notes.openai: Internationally active gallery pairing significant modernist estates with research-driven contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Operating since 1974, a Bay Area institution showing Robert Colescott, Hung Liu, Rigo 23 and self-taught artists alongside emerging talent.
notes.openai: A cornerstone of San Francisco contemporary art, noted for diverse artists and decades of institutional engagement.

galleries.name: CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts

notes.anthropic: The Bay Area's most intellectually influential kunsthalle-style exhibition and research space, with a curatorial fellowship pipeline and internationally followed programme.
notes.openai: Internationally influential curatorial and research institute known for experimental exhibitions, publications and artist commissions.

names.anthropic: CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts
names.openai: CCA Wattis Institute for Contemporary Arts

notes.anthropic: Founded 1996; a leading champion of Black artists and photography — Gordon Parks, Ming Smith, Lava Thomas — with a Brooklyn project space and strong fair presence.
notes.openai: Nationally influential Black-owned gallery with a socially engaged programme and strong museum and fair presence.

notes.anthropic: Chris Perez's gallery has shaped two decades of Bay Area contemporary practice, showing Ruth Laskey, Mitzi Pederson, Takeshi Murata and Jordan Kantor.
notes.openai: Highly regarded for introducing experimental artists and sustaining a distinctive, critically followed programme.

notes.anthropic: Photography-forward programme (formerly Casemore Kirkeby) with artists such as Klea McKenna, Lucas Blalock and John Chiara; a critical hub for lens-based work.
notes.openai: Critically regarded gallery advancing expanded photography, moving image and other lens-based contemporary practices.

notes.anthropic: Since 1974 the city's key artist-centred nonprofit: juried and curated exhibitions, Alternative Exposure grants and generations of Bay Area artists' first shows.
notes.openai: Seminal artist-centered nonprofit supporting experimental work, commissions and emerging Bay Area voices since 1974.

notes.anthropic: Founded 2019 by a veteran of the city's leading galleries; a well-reviewed programme of emerging and mid-career artists with growing fair visibility.
notes.openai: Agile contemporary programme supporting emerging and mid-career artists through focused exhibitions and fairs.

notes.anthropic: Beloved basement gallery under a Chinatown shop; scrappy, curatorially adventurous and disproportionately influential on the city's younger scene.
notes.openai: Artist-founded gallery admired for unconventional presentations and an influential emerging and experimental programme.

galleries.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts

notes.anthropic: Non-collecting multidisciplinary arts centre; decades of major commissions, the Bay Area Now survey and civic-scale contemporary programming.
notes.openai: Major multidisciplinary contemporary-arts institution presenting ambitious exhibitions, commissions and civic programming.

names.anthropic: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
names.openai: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts

notes.anthropic: Grown out of Friends Indeed; a nimble, internationally connected dealer with New York collaborations and a sharply curated emerging roster.
notes.openai: Fast-rising gallery with an international, cross-generational programme and expanding art-fair visibility.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1984; experimental sound, performance and installation programming in a landmark Redstone Building space, with an internationally respected commissioning record.
notes.openai: Historic experimental-art organization supporting risk-taking installation, sound, performance and time-based work.

notes.anthropic: Martin Muller's gallery since 1979, mixing Russian avant-garde and European modernism with contemporary figures such as Mel Ramos and Gottfried Helnwein.
notes.openai: A long-lived gallery with scholarly modernist holdings and a substantial programme of international contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Griff Williams's gallery and Urban Digital Color press; thirty years of editions and exhibitions with Rex Ray, Amy Ellingson and Chris Johanson.
notes.openai: Veteran gallery and print publisher with a distinctive interdisciplinary programme and deep Bay Area roots.

notes.anthropic: Long-established dealer in vintage and contemporary photography, from the Russian avant-garde to contemporary lens-based artists.
notes.openai: Internationally respected photography gallery spanning historic avant-gardes and important contemporary practitioners.

galleries.name: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco

notes.anthropic: Contemporary Asian and Asian American programming through its Hilton-level galleries, 41 Ross and Edge on the Square; a leading voice in community-based contemporary art.
notes.openai: Nationally important platform for contemporary Chinese and Asian diasporic art, community history and public commissions.

names.anthropic: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco
names.openai: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco

notes.anthropic: Andrew McClintock's gallery pairs Bay Area conceptual legacies with young international artists; active on the fair circuit and in artist publishing.
notes.openai: Known for adventurous exhibitions that connect younger Bay Area practices with wider contemporary-art conversations.

notes.anthropic: Longstanding dealer of Bay Area emerging and mid-career artists, with an eye for craft-inflected and narrative painting.
notes.openai: Respected local gallery with a strong record of developing Bay Area painters and interdisciplinary artists.

notes.anthropic: Curator-driven gallery known for launching Bay Area artists such as Chelsea Ryoko Wong and Rachelle Bussières into wider institutional attention.
notes.openai: Independent programme supporting socially engaged, feminist and interdisciplinary artists through exhibitions and special projects.

notes.anthropic: Painting-focused Union Square gallery open since 1997, with a consistent stable of contemporary figurative and abstract painters.
notes.openai: Prominent downtown gallery with a durable programme centered on contemporary painting, sculpture and photography.

notes.anthropic: Abstraction-focused programme with international mid-career artists; a steady presence at Minnesota Street Project and West Coast fairs.
notes.openai: Established gallery representing accomplished Bay Area and international artists across painting, sculpture and installation.

notes.anthropic: Custodian of Wayne Thiebaud's legacy plus a select group of Bay Area representational painters and printmakers.
notes.openai: Respected, long-running gallery known for exacting presentations of American painting, sculpture and works on paper.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1974; a historic nonprofit for experimental lens-based practice, publications and emerging photographers.
notes.openai: Historic nonprofit photography organization supporting emerging artists, critical discourse and expanded lens-based media.

notes.anthropic: Nonprofit exhibition space and residency emphasising research-driven and socially engaged projects by Bay Area and international artists.
notes.openai: Artist-run space presenting critically engaged exhibitions by emerging and established artists in an intimate setting.

notes.anthropic: Monique Deschaines's photography-driven gallery, showing artists like Meghann Riepenhoff and Ian van Coller with strong fair and museum traction.
notes.openai: Curatorially focused gallery recognized for experimental photography, abstraction and materially sensitive practices.

notes.anthropic: Two decades of championing outsider, visionary and idiosyncratic contemporary work that few other SF galleries would show.
notes.openai: Idiosyncratic programme championing self-taught, outsider-adjacent and formally inventive contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Studio and gallery for artists with developmental disabilities since 1983; its artists now appear in museum collections and commercial galleries worldwide.
notes.openai: Internationally recognized studio and gallery advancing artists with developmental disabilities and disability-led cultural discourse.

notes.anthropic: Since 1987 a crucible of Mission School and street-derived practice (Barry McGee, Margaret Kilgallen) plus a long-running new-music series.
notes.openai: Foundational artist-run nonprofit associated with experimental visual art, sound and performance in the Tenderloin.

notes.anthropic: Curated, thematically organised exhibitions with an emphasis on photography and cross-cultural Asian–American dialogues.
notes.openai: Long-running gallery, formerly Modernbook, with particular strength in contemporary photography and works on paper.

notes.anthropic: The subsidised gallery and studio complex that reorganised the SF art map after the 49 Geary exodus; also mounts its own foundation exhibitions.
notes.openai: Produces independent exhibitions and commissions in the complex's shared spaces while strengthening San Francisco's gallery ecosystem.

notes.anthropic: Big-tent civic arts centre with curatorial residencies, the annual Día de los Muertos exhibition and decades of community-rooted contemporary shows.
notes.openai: Large civic arts venue supporting culturally diverse, community-rooted and experimental contemporary exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Studio-plus-gallery nonprofit linking artist residencies to arts education; a key entry point for emerging Bay Area artists.
notes.openai: Artist-run nonprofit combining ambitious exhibitions with studios, education and career support for emerging artists.

notes.anthropic: Leading new-contemporary/illustrative gallery with New York and Los Angeles branches; large young collector base.
notes.openai: Widely followed gallery connecting technically accomplished emerging artists with international collectors and fairs.
Long-established dealer with an influential programme spanning important international and Bay Area contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Opened 2023 with a mission to platform BIPOC and LGBTQ+ artists; among the most watched recent additions to the SF gallery scene.
notes.openai: Distinctive new programme foregrounding queer, Black and diasporic artists historically underrepresented by commercial galleries.

galleries.name: 500 Capp Street Foundation (The David Ireland House)

notes.anthropic: David Ireland's conceptual house-artwork preserved as a public site with commissions and residencies by contemporary artists.
notes.openai: Preserves David Ireland's landmark house while commissioning contemporary artists to engage its conceptual and architectural legacy.

names.anthropic: 500 Capp Street Foundation (The David Ireland House)

notes.anthropic: San Francisco Arts Commission's exhibition programme in the Veterans Building and Main Library, giving civic platform to Bay Area contemporary artists.
notes.openai: Municipal gallery programme commissioning contemporary work and giving public visibility to diverse Bay Area artists.

notes.anthropic: Operating since 1982; a durable SoMa space showing mid-career Bay Area painters and sculptors to corporate and private collections.
notes.openai: Long-running commercial gallery with broad support for contemporary Bay Area painting, sculpture and photography.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1970, the historic engine of Chicano/Latinx contemporary art in the Bay Area, from Ester Hernández to today's digital mural projects.
notes.openai: Landmark Chicano and Latino arts organization with a major legacy of politically engaged exhibitions and public art.

notes.anthropic: The only mega-gallery with a permanent San Francisco outpost (opened 2016), bringing blue-chip international programming to the Bay Area.
Art-and-technology nonprofit in the Grand Theater; festivals, immersive commissions and a leading platform for digital and new-media art.
notes.openai: Influential nonprofit at the intersection of art, technology, design and civic experimentation.

notes.anthropic: Successor to Gallery Paule Anglim (est. 1970s), the keeper of Bay Area conceptual and Funk legacies: Deborah Oropallo, William T. Wiley, Tony Labat, Nathaniel Dorsky estate artists.
Large warehouse space with a rigorous international programme — Jim Campbell, Emil Lukas, Liliana Porter, Alan Rath estate — and long fair participation.
Small artist-organised space in a working upholstery shop, known for tightly curated, experimental exhibitions.
notes.openai: Artist-organized space with a critically noticed programme of unconventional, research-led exhibitions.

galleries.name: Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco

notes.anthropic: Free, non-collecting kunsthalle opened 2022 that has quickly become a major platform for local and international contemporary artists.

names.anthropic: Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco

notes.anthropic: Legendary bookstore back room where the Mission School and countless young artists showed first; still a barometer of the underground scene.
notes.openai: Storied artist-run gallery embedded in Adobe Books and central to generations of Mission art culture.
Thoughtful contemporary programme emphasizing material experimentation, cultural exchange and underrecognized practices.
Long-standing contemporary gallery known for conceptually oriented painting, sculpture and interdisciplinary work.

galleries.name: Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts

notes.anthropic: Community anchor since 1977 with gallery exhibitions and the Mission Gráfica print studio, a key site for Latinx contemporary practice.
notes.openai: Historic Latino cultural center with substantial gallery exhibitions, printmaking and community arts programming.

names.anthropic: Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts
names.openai: Mission Cultural Center for Latino Arts

notes.anthropic: North Beach fixture for figurative, surrealist and craft-based contemporary work with a strong group-show tradition.
notes.openai: Prominent platform for figurative, surrealist and pop-influenced contemporary art with an international following.

notes.anthropic: Pilara Foundation's vast free-admission photography exhibition space, one of the largest in the world and a magnet for scholars and collectors.

notes.openai: Growing international programme that brings artists from Asia and its diasporas into dialogue with Bay Area audiences.

notes.anthropic: Young Mission gallery focused on emerging Bay Area painters, with an accessible, community-facing exhibition model.
notes.openai: Community-minded gallery promoting emerging and mid-career Bay Area artists through exhibitions and public initiatives.
Artist-run programme offering an important testing ground for emerging artists and experimental exhibition formats.

notes.anthropic: Neighbourhood gallery west of Twin Peaks with a serious, artist-run sensibility and a following for Bay Area abstraction and ceramics.
notes.openai: Independent neighborhood gallery with a consistent programme of contemporary painting, photography and mixed media.
Compact but influential gallery admired for precise exhibitions of emerging conceptual and materially driven art.

notes.anthropic: Longstanding Black cultural centre presenting contemporary exhibitions, residencies and performance in the historic Fillmore.
notes.openai: Essential Black cultural institution presenting contemporary exhibitions alongside performance and community programming.
Veteran photography specialist with deep holdings and exhibitions spanning canonical and contemporary West Coast work.

notes.anthropic: Hybrid gallery-bar operating since 1993; an early platform for street-derived and underground SF artists.
notes.openai: Long-lived hybrid gallery and cultural venue important to San Francisco's independent art and illustration communities.
Established dealer presenting materially ambitious contemporary painting, sculpture, textiles and socially engaged work.
Specialized venue for new media, moving image, digital culture and technologically engaged contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Idiosyncratic ramped space in a former mortuary hosting emerging artists, installation and performance.
notes.openai: Artist-run nonprofit using a distinctive ramped space for experimental exhibitions and emerging curatorial voices.

notes.anthropic: Specialist in West Coast minimalism, Light and Space and geometric abstraction; represents artists including John Zurier and Peter Alexander's circle.
Design-store-with-gallery that has shown a generation of Bay Area artists and publishes small-run artist editions and books.
notes.openai: Influential independent gallery and art-book venue with deep ties to Bay Area artists, publishing and visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Union Square dealer in modern and contemporary blue-chip names, from Kounellis and Botero to Chihuly and Zhang Huan.
notes.openai: Internationally oriented gallery with a long record of postwar and contemporary exhibitions in downtown San Francisco.

notes.anthropic: Outer Sunset gallery centred on surf, landscape and photographic culture; the west side's most consistent exhibition venue.
notes.openai: Artist-run Outer Sunset venue connecting contemporary exhibitions with the neighborhood's coastal culture and ecology.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run gallery and studio building with juried national exhibitions and a strong local membership base.
notes.openai: Artist-run gallery and studio complex presenting juried exhibitions and independent Bay Area practices.

notes.anthropic: The pioneering dump residency (since 1990) with public exhibitions of work made from discarded materials; internationally imitated.

notes.openai: Long-running artist-run center for experimental film, video, installation, performance and independent media.
Artist-led venue gaining attention for experimental exhibitions, performances and cross-disciplinary community programming.
Young gallery presenting materially adventurous work by emerging artists in focused, curatorially alert exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Small but respected new-media nonprofit presenting experimental digital, networked and time-based work.

notes.openai: Contemporary gallery known for accessible but serious presentations of emerging, women and diasporic artists.

notes.anthropic: Nonprofit gallery and studio centring older adults and disability-inclusive contemporary practice, with a professionally curated programme.
notes.openai: Intergenerational arts nonprofit presenting exhibitions that connect contemporary practice, aging and community participation.
Expanding contemporary programme focused on technically accomplished painting, sculpture and mixed-media practices.
Established gallery presenting postwar and contemporary abstraction, sculpture and internationally oriented exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Since 1983, a commercially strong programme of European and American contemporary painting and sculpture with a St Helena branch.

notes.openai: Large contemporary venue known for immersive installations, mural culture and technically elaborate figurative work.
Independent exhibition space presenting ambitious installations and crossover projects by local and international artists.

notes.anthropic: Pop-surrealist and film-inflected gallery known for blockbuster themed shows and a national following.
Contemporary programme spanning painting, ceramics and design-adjacent work by emerging Bay Area and international artists.
Large downtown operation dealing in surrealism and modern masters alongside contemporary figuration; a high-traffic commercial presence.
notes.openai: Substantial private gallery combining modern masters with contemporary figurative and surrealist-oriented artists.

notes.anthropic: Sculpture and collectible-design programme in Jackson Square, bridging fine art and studio furniture with museum-quality presentation.

galleries.name: Juan R. Fuentes Gallery at Acción Latina

notes.openai: Important Mission venue for contemporary Latino, Indigenous, activist and community-based visual art.

names.openai: Juan R. Fuentes Gallery at Acción Latina

notes.openai: Durable artist cooperative providing an accessible exhibition platform for a broad cross-section of local artists.
Significant community gallery supporting Tenderloin artists and expanding access for people affected by poverty and homelessness.
Independent arts organization producing exhibitions, residencies and public conversations around creative practice and social inquiry.

galleries.name: Thacher Gallery, University of San Francisco

notes.anthropic: Free public university gallery with socially engaged, faith- and justice-themed contemporary exhibitions and Bay Area artist commissions.

names.anthropic: Thacher Gallery, University of San Francisco

notes.openai: Neighborhood contemporary gallery with a sustained commitment to Bay Area artists and Outer Sunset cultural life.

galleries.name: Fine Arts Gallery, San Francisco State University

notes.anthropic: Long-running academic gallery presenting contemporary group exhibitions and Bay Area artists to a wide public audience.

names.anthropic: Fine Arts Gallery, San Francisco State University

notes.openai: Long-running gallery devoted to contemporary Bay Area artists across painting, sculpture, photography and works on paper.

galleries.name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture (Gallery 308)

notes.anthropic: Waterfront arts campus whose Gallery 308 and Festival Pavilion host large-scale contemporary exhibitions and commissions.

names.anthropic: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture (Gallery 308)

notes.openai: Photography-oriented gallery emphasizing humanitarian, environmental and socially engaged visual storytelling.

notes.anthropic: Warehouse arts complex with a gallery and residency programme bridging music, immersive installation and visual art.

notes.openai: Independent photography gallery presenting contemporary lens-based artists and historically informed exhibitions.
Long-established downtown gallery dealing in modern and contemporary painting, sculpture and editioned work.

notes.anthropic: Private dealership and exhibition space handling postwar California artists and estates, with strong secondary-market scholarship.
The world's pioneering studio and gallery for artists with disabilities (since 1974); its artists are in MoMA, SFMOMA and the Pompidou.
Printmaking and media residency centre with an active gallery; a four-decade fixture of Bay Area artist development.

notes.openai: Mission gallery supporting local contemporary art, illustration, environmental themes and urban visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Fine-art print publisher and gallery producing editions with Martin Puryear, Kerry James Marshall and the Gee's Bend quilters.

notes.openai: Contemporary gallery presenting abstraction, sculpture and nature-oriented work by established and emerging artists.

notes.anthropic: Long-running East Bay gallery with a conceptually grounded roster and consistent art-fair participation.

notes.openai: Artist-led exhibition initiative known for inclusive group shows, community organizing and support for Bay Area artists.

notes.anthropic: One of the East Bay's most visible young galleries, showing emerging painters with national fair presence.

galleries.name: San Francisco Center for the Book

notes.openai: Nationally respected book-arts organization with public exhibitions devoted to artists' books, printing and related contemporary practices.

names.openai: San Francisco Center for the Book

notes.anthropic: Uptown Oakland gallery known for material-driven, offbeat contemporary work since 2006.

notes.openai: Exhibits major contemporary artists through one of the country's most distinguished traditions of artist-book publishing.

notes.anthropic: Tiny curator-run nonprofit with an outsized critical reputation for focused, experimental solo projects.

notes.openai: Produces ambitious site-responsive contemporary projects addressing place, history, landscape and public life.

notes.anthropic: Since 1974 the East Bay's main artist-service nonprofit, running the Open Studios and a commons-model exhibition programme.

notes.openai: Dedicated public platform for LGBTQ+ artists, bringing contemporary queer visual art into the heart of the Castro.

notes.anthropic: Live Oak Park nonprofit presenting contemporary Bay Area exhibitions and public programmes for more than fifty years.

notes.openai: Compact artist-run window space presenting experimental installations continuously to Valencia Street pedestrians.

notes.anthropic: Progressive studio and gallery for disabled artists whose programme has gained major curatorial attention nationally.

notes.openai: Bay Area gallery with a polished programme of contemporary abstraction, figuration and materially driven work.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run cooperative gallery, a durable node of Oakland's Art Murmur ecosystem.

notes.openai: Emerging gallery supporting younger artists and accessible contemporary programming in the Tenderloin.

notes.anthropic: Small West Oakland gallery with a steady programme of Bay Area painting, sculpture and works on paper.

notes.openai: Young contemporary gallery building attention around emerging artists and cross-cultural, internationally minded exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Gallery, studios and an art-subscription programme that has broadened access to collecting emerging Bay Area artists.

notes.openai: Historic women-led organization maintaining a public contemporary gallery and broad exhibition opportunities for Bay Area artists.
